cases.name: einstein.minkowski_vanishes
cases.notes: constant metric, so every stencil sums to exactly zero -- an exactness claim
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} = 0 in flat Cartesian coordinates

cases.name: einstein.flat_spherical_vanishes
cases.notes: measured 6.7e-3; the case where a coordinate connection would become false stress-energy. Boundary worst = 0.088224
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} = 0 for flat space in ANY chart, despite Gamma != 0

cases.name: einstein.schwarzschild_vanishes
cases.notes: measured 1.7e-3
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} = 0 (vacuum Einstein equation)

cases.name: einstein.schwarzschild_still_curved
cases.notes: a vanishing Einstein tensor is not a vanishing curvature; without this the case above would be satisfied by a pipeline that returns zero
cases.reference: K = 48 M^2 / r^6 remains nonzero where G vanishes

cases.name: einstein.square_chart_independent
cases.notes: both are near zero for a vacuum; the de Sitter group carries the same test with a nonzero value
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} G^{mu nu} is a scalar and agrees between charts

cases.name: einstein.desitter_analytic_value
cases.notes: measured 2.9e-2. NOTE the sign: with R_{mu nu} = +(3/L^2) g and R = +12/L^2, G = R_{mu nu} - g R/2 = (3/L^2 - 6/L^2) g = -(3/L^2) g
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} = -(3/L^2) g_{mu nu} for static de Sitter

cases.name: einstein.desitter_vacuum_with_lambda
cases.notes: the case that separates the GEOMETRIC Einstein tensor from MATTER stress-energy: G is large here, yet the spacetime contains nothing
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} + Lambda g_{mu nu} = 0 with Lambda = 3/L^2

cases.name: einstein.desitter_matter_and_lambda_sources_differ
cases.notes: de Sitter contains no matter and is nonetheless sourced. Reporting a single 'the stress-energy' number here would have to pick one of these two and would be wrong about the other
cases.reference: T^matter vanishes for de Sitter while T^Lambda does not

cases.name: einstein.alcubierre_vs_symbolic
cases.notes: worst at (2.000000,0.000000,0.000000) component 22; the reference assembles G from ITS OWN symbolic Ricci, never from this pipeline. Measured 1.2e-2 -- O(h^2), inherited from the Ricci tensor it is built from
cases.reference: G_{mu nu} componentwise against exact symbolic differentiation

cases.name: einstein.g00_is_not_an_energy_density
cases.notes: G_00 is POSITIVE across the sampled points for this configuration. That is not a statement that the inferred source has positive energy density: an energy density is T_{mu nu} u^mu u^nu for a specified normalised observer, which A6 introduces and A5 does not have. No output of A5 may be labelled an energy density
cases.reference: G_00 is a coordinate component, not an observer-measured scalar

cases.name: einstein.raw_antisymmetry_measured
cases.notes: measured 4.7e-3, inherited from the O(h^2) Ricci asymmetry A4 traced to the discrete product rule. Reported rather than hidden: symmetrising in place would destroy the only direct measure of how far the discretisation is from the continuum. Convergence is demonstrated separately
cases.reference: max |G_{mu nu} - G_{nu mu}| on the directly computed tensor

cases.name: einstein.symmetric_projection_is_symmetric
cases.notes: exact in floating point: a + b and b + a are the same expression, so the halved sum is bit-identical either way round
cases.reference: (1/2)(G + G^T) is exactly symmetric

cases.name: einstein.raw_and_symmetric_both_available
cases.notes: if this ever reads zero, the raw tensor has been silently symmetrised and the antisymmetry measurement above is vacuous
cases.reference: the raw tensor is preserved alongside its symmetric projection

cases.name: einstein.trace_identity
cases.notes: algebraic: g^{mu nu}(R_{mu nu} - g_{mu nu} R/2) = R - 4R/2 = -R, using g^{mu nu} g_{mu nu} = 4. Roundoff, not truncation -- it needs no product rule and holds for whatever R_{mu nu} the discretisation produced
cases.reference: G^mu_mu = -R in four dimensions

cases.computed_description: Schwarzschild: max|G| = 0.031160, |div G| = 0.000000, relative = 0.000000;  Alcubierre: max|G| = 0.139083, |div G| = 0.005993, relative = 0.043088
cases.expected_description: the geometry with the smaller |G| has the smaller absolute residual
cases.name: bianchi.absolute_residual_is_not_enough
cases.notes: a vacuum would otherwise appear to satisfy the contracted Bianchi identity better than a curved spacetime, purely because there is less of everything to be wrong about
cases.reference: the absolute divergence tracks the size of G, not the quality of the identity

cases.name: bianchi.contracted_residual_absolute
cases.notes: NOT an exact finite-difference identity: it needs a third nested derivative pass and the product rule. max|G| = 0.139083. Interior only, shell depth 3 -- the divergence is contaminated three points deep
cases.reference: nabla_mu G^{mu nu} = 0, absolute

cases.name: bianchi.contracted_residual_relative
cases.notes: the meaningful measure: an absolute residual can be made arbitrarily small by choosing a geometry with little curvature
cases.reference: nabla_mu G^{mu nu} = 0, normalised by max |G_{mu nu}|

cases.name: einstein.antisymmetry_converges
cases.notes: order 17->25 = 2.124725. This is what licenses treating the antisymmetry as truncation error rather than as a defect, and what makes the symmetric projection legitimate rather than a cover-up
cases.reference: the antisymmetric part of G falls as O(h^2)

cases.name: bianchi.converges
cases.notes: order 17->25 = 0.890315. A wide band is asserted deliberately: the divergence is a THIRD nested derivative, so at these grids it carries more pre-asymptotic error than any other quantity in the project. What matters is that it converges at all -- a non-converging Bianchi residual would mean the Einstein tensor is wrong
cases.reference: the contracted Bianchi residual falls under refinement

cases.name: units.geometrized_conversion
cases.notes: the conversion the A5 gate verifies; SI is a presentation layer on top of it
cases.reference: T_{mu nu} = G_{mu nu} / (8 pi) in geometrized units

cases.name: units.si_requires_an_explicit_scale
cases.notes: a grid coordinate is a pure number, not metres. Multiplying a dimensionless curvature by c^4/(8 pi G_N) and printing J/m^3 is the standard way to produce a confidently wrong number
cases.reference: no SI value is produced without a declared coordinate scale

cases.name: units.si_conversion_dimensional_consistency
cases.reference: T^SI = c^4/(8 pi G_N) * G_dimensionless / L0^2

cases.name: units.si_scales_as_inverse_length_squared
cases.notes: the physical content of the conversion: the same dimensionless geometry means a very different source depending on how big you declare it to be
cases.reference: T^SI scales as 1/L0^2

cases.computed_description: curvature was refused: temporal policy is Refused: FrozenTimeDiagnostic discards d_0 g -- curvature built from a discarded temporal derivative is not the curvature of any spacetime
cases.name: einstein.frozen_time_refused
cases.notes: the refusal propagates: A5 does not re-derive it, it inherits it
cases.reference: no Einstein tensor is produced from a discarded temporal derivative

cases.name: einstein.deterministic
cases.notes: no ordering, threading or accumulation nondeterminism in the assembly
cases.reference: two identical runs produce bit-identical tensors

cases.computed_description: A5 computes the geometric Einstein tensor and the stress-energy tensor inferred through Einstein's equation for the selected metric. It does not establish that this source can be generated physically, that energy conditions are satisfied, or that FTL travel is realizable.
cases.name: einstein.scope_statement_recorded
cases.reference: every A5 report carries its scope limitation

cases.name: lambda.matter_source_identity
cases.notes: the identity A5 named correctly and computed as if it were the Lambda source
cases.reference: 8 pi T^matter = G + Lambda g

cases.name: lambda.effective_lambda_source_identity
cases.notes: NOTE THE SIGN. This is the tensor A5's enum claimed to produce; it differs from what A5 computed by more than a sign, since that was G + Lambda g
cases.reference: 8 pi T^Lambda = -Lambda g

cases.name: lambda.total_source_identity
cases.notes: independent of Lambda, as it must be: moving Lambda between the two sides of the field equation is bookkeeping, not physics
cases.reference: 8 pi T^total = G

cases.name: lambda.decomposition_closure
cases.notes: the closure that makes the decomposition a decomposition rather than three unrelated fields
cases.reference: T^total = T^matter + T^Lambda

cases.name: lambda.desitter_matter_source_vanishes
cases.notes: the physical content of the correction. A5's mislabelled field computed exactly this quantity while calling it the Lambda source, so a reader would have concluded de Sitter's Lambda source was zero
cases.reference: T^matter = 0 for de Sitter with Lambda = 3/L^2: it is a VACUUM

cases.name: lambda.desitter_lambda_source_nonzero
cases.notes: expected Lambda/(8 pi) times the metric scale, i.e. about 0.029842
cases.reference: T^Lambda != 0 for de Sitter

cases.name: lambda.desitter_total_equals_lambda_source
cases.reference: T^total = T^Lambda for de Sitter, because T^matter vanishes

cases.name: lambda.zero_lambda_source_vanishes
cases.notes: multiplication by a literal zero, so exact rather than small
cases.reference: T^Lambda = 0 exactly when Lambda = 0

cases.name: lambda.zero_lambda_matter_equals_total
cases.notes: the warp-drive case: with no cosmological constant the decomposition collapses to the single tensor A5 reported, which is why the A5 numerical results are unaffected by this correction
cases.reference: T^matter = T^total = G/(8 pi) when Lambda = 0

cases.computed_description: G_{mu nu} + Lambda g_{mu nu} = 8 pi T^matter_{mu nu}; T^Lambda = -Lambda g/(8 pi); T^total = T^matter + T^Lambda = G/(8 pi)
cases.expected_description: convention string names the implemented decomposition
cases.name: lambda.labels_match_arithmetic
cases.notes: the A5C requirement in one sentence: no name may assert one physical interpretation while the arithmetic implements another
cases.reference: the recorded convention states the equation actually implemented

cases.expected_description: SourceDecomposition with four separately named tensors
cases.name: lambda.no_ambiguous_policy_remains
cases.notes: CosmologicalConstantTreatment and its LambdaAsEffectiveStressEnergy member are removed, not renamed: an enum cannot express a decomposition, and a caller that could select one tensor would still have to guess which one it received
cases.reference: the public API exposes no single policy-selected 'the source' field

cases.name: lambda.deterministic_records
cases.notes: exact equality required
cases.reference: two identical runs give bit-identical decompositions

title: Einstein tensor and inferred stress-energy: G = R_{mu nu} - g R / 2, raw and symmetric, its trace and square, the contracted Bianchi residual, cosmological-constant treatment and the units layer
